maria_support: Hey team — customer PYL-34 reporting alerts firing every 1m even though dashboard shows flat metrics. They say thresholds are noisy since yesterday morning. :confused:
kevin_sre: Can you paste the alert rule and the panel query?
maria_support: Alert rule: `threshold(alert_rate, > 0.5, for: 2m)` Panel is a timeseries over `sum(requests) by service` with `date_histogram` 1m. Customer provided screenshot, I'll attach in ticket.
tasha_eng-platform: Hm 1m buckets + alert backend does its own rollup to 5m sometimes, that mismatch can cause flapping. Did the customer recently change their dashboard timefield?
maria_support: They said they switched to `ingest_time` for testing last week. Could that explain it?
kevin_sre: Yes — alerts use event_time by default. If dashboard uses ingest_time and alerting engine uses event_time you can get off-by-window issues, especially when data arrives late. We saw similar with delayed VPC logs.
sam_prod_analytics: Quick repro idea: send a synthetic event with event_time = t and ingest_time = t+90s, then query `date_histogram` on both fields.
kevin_sre: Good call. Maria can you ask customer for a short ingestion sample or share a query to pull `min(event_time), min(ingest_time)` per shard?
maria_support: Asked and they provided a CSV snippet. Attaching in ticket.
kevin_sre: Alright I ran a local repro against their dataset. Confirmed: dashboard panels built on `ingest_time` show spikes at different bucket boundaries than alert engine which uses `event_time` when available. That causes alerts to see transient >0.5 spikes that the dashboard smooths out.
tasha_eng-platform: We should make the mismatch more visible in the console. Suggestion: show the panel's timefield next to alert preview and warn if timefield differs from alert engine timefield.
sam_prod_analytics: Also consider having alert engine accept an override toggle to use `ingest_time` when event_time is absent to match dashboard behavior.
kevin_sre: Mitigation for customer: change alert to use a longer `for` window (5m) or set alert to evaluate on `ingest_time` (if supported) and temporarily mute noisy alerts. For now I recommend increasing `for` and lowering alert sensitivity.
maria_support: Customer accepted increasing `for` to 5m but asked for a permanent fix.
tasha_eng-platform: Filed ENG-8021 to add a console hint and an opt-in alert timefield selector.
kevin_sre: I also added a short-term guard in the alerting service: if the dashboard timefield != alert timefield and bucket size < 2m, log a warning and attach bucket-mapping diagnostic to the alert execution trace.
infra-bot: deploy-bot has queued a canary with ID canary-227 for review.
kevin_sre: Canary deployed to staging. I ran the repro script and attached logs to ENG-8021.
maria_support: Customer please confirm once alerts quiet down after the config change. :raised_hands:
customer_PYL-34: confirmed in thread — noise reduced after increasing `for` and aligning timefield. Thanks! :thumbsup:
kevin_sre: Follow-ups: (1) add console hint, (2) docs for timefield mismatch and recommended patterns, (3) consider alert engine opt-in for ingest_time. I'll own (2) and (3), Tasha will own (1).
tasha_eng-platform: Ack. I'll include a UX mock and a small banner text for the alert creation flow.
maria_support: Closing loop with customer and marking ticket as workaround applied. Will update once ENG-8021 lands.
sam_prod_analytics: Filed a small internal runbook for support with repro steps and the SQL snippet used for diagnosis: ```SELECT service, min(event_time) AS min_ev, min(ingest_time) AS min_ing, count(*) FROM metrics WHERE $__timeFilter(event_time) GROUP BY service;```
kevin_sre: Nice. Adding one more note — when data ingestion has jitter > bucket size, prefer event_time bucketing for correctness, or increase bucket size.
maria_support: Thanks all, moving to resolved unless anything else pops up. :white_check_mark:
